description: P5.1 IPC + state plumbing AND the supporting Rust #[tauri::command] additions every surface needs. This is the shared foundation the five surfaces build on, so it lands first. Complete the typed invoke wrappers (src/ipc/commands.ts) and the Zustand stores (src/state/{conversations,providers,tools,personas}.ts), treating the core as authoritative and refreshing/invalidating caches on the relevant CoreEvents (Section 7.3). Add the missing Rust command handlers (get_messages, set_conversation_route, set_message_override seam, assign_persona, MCP server CRUD + set_mcp_enabled + refresh_mcp_tools + set_tool_permission, export_conversation, open_conversation, get_route_explanation, stop_generation) with argument validation, the _inner testability pattern, and unit tests, register them in generate_handler!, and add a runtime MCP handle manager to AppState so servers connect/disconnect and emit mcp_state_changed/mcp_error. Keep additions minimal and scoped to what Section 8 surfaces need; do not build Phase 6 hardening. NOTE: `zustand` is not yet a dependency and node_modules cannot be installed in the sandbox (npm 403), but CI runs `npm install` (no lockfile) so a newly declared dependency resolves on CI; add `zustand` to package.json dependencies.
steps: Add `zustand` (^4 or ^5, pick a version compatible with React 18) to `dependencies` in hybrid-orchestrator/frontend/package.json. Do NOT attempt `npm install` locally (registry 403); CI installs it. If you prefer to avoid a new dependency entirely, implement a tiny local store helper instead and document the choice in findings, but the briefing/tasks call for Zustand stores, so prefer zustand.

RUST: In crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs add these #[tauri::command] handlers, each following the existing style (borrow AppState, validate args with parse_uuid/validate_nonempty/validate_manual_route/bounds, delegate, return Result<_, CommandError>), and extract an `_inner` body for testability where a live tauri::State would otherwise block a unit test: get_messages(conversationId) -> Vec<Message> via session_manager.list_messages; set_conversation_route(conversationId, route: Option<ManualRoute>) via session_manager.set_conversation_route (validate route when Some); assign_persona(conversationId, personaId: Option<String>) via session_manager.assign_persona; get_route_explanation(conversationId) -> a small DisplaySafe struct { rationale, providerId, model, source } by resolving the active conversation pref/persona through the routing PolicyRegistry candidate set (reuse the registry/available-model assembly already in list_available_models_inner/send_message_inner; if a full dry-run route is too heavy, return the last persisted message route metadata or a computed preview — keep it display-safe, never secrets).

RUST: MCP server management commands backed by persistence::McpServerRepo (insert/get/list/update/delete already exist) and a NEW runtime handle manager. list_mcp_servers() -> Vec<McpServerConfig>; add_mcp_server(config: McpServerInput) -> McpServerConfig (assign Uuid, validate name/transport fields with bounds, insert, then connect if enabled); update_mcp_server(id, config) (validate, update row, reconnect handle); remove_mcp_server(id) (teardown handle, delete row); set_mcp_enabled(id, enabled: bool) (connect/teardown handle + persist enabled); refresh_mcp_tools(id) (handle.reconnect or re-list tools) -> Vec<ToolDescriptor-display-safe>; set_tool_permission(serverId, toolName: Option<String>, mode: PermissionMode) — persist per-server permission mode via the McpServerConfig.permission_mode (and, for per-tool overrides, store them; if per-tool override persistence does not exist yet, scope this command to the per-server permission_mode and note the per-tool-override limitation in findings rather than inventing a new schema). Validate transport fields: stdio requires non-empty command; httpSse requires a non-empty url. env/headers are Vec<(String,String)> — mirror the existing McpTransport serde exactly.

RUST: Add a runtime MCP handle manager to AppState (src/state.rs). Today `mcp_servers: Arc<Vec<Arc<McpServerHandle>>>` is a fixed empty Vec. Replace/augment with a shared, mutable registry (e.g. Arc<Mutex<HashMap<Uuid, Arc<McpServerHandle>>>> or an Arc<RwLock<...>>) so the new commands can add/remove/reconnect handles at runtime and send_message can read the current connected set. On AppState::initialize, load persisted McpServerConfig rows and connect the enabled ones (spawn connects; do NOT block startup on a slow/broken server — connect in the background and let mcp_state_changed/mcp_error events report status). Ensure send_message_inner reads the live connected-handle set instead of the empty Vec. Emit CoreEvent::McpStateChanged / McpError as handles connect/disconnect (McpServerHandle exposes state()/connect()/reconnect()/teardown()). Keep the AppState::new (test) constructor compiling.

RUST: export_conversation(conversationId, format: ExportFormat) -> String. ExportFormat is a small serde enum (e.g. { markdown, json }) with per-variant camelCase; assemble the conversation + its messages (session_manager.get_conversation + list_messages) into a Markdown or JSON string. Display-safe only. open_conversation(conversationId) -> Conversation: load and return the full conversation so the UI can restore persona/route pin/tags/enabled tools (Section 8.5 resume); if a richer resume payload is needed, return a small struct bundling the Conversation plus its messages — keep it minimal. stop_generation(conversationId) -> (): wire to whatever cancellation seam exists for an in-flight turn; if the pipeline has no cancellation handle yet, implement a best-effort cancel-flag registry on AppState keyed by conversationId that run_turn checks, OR, if that is out of scope, make stop_generation a validated no-op that returns Ok(()) and document the limitation in findings (the UI still needs the command to exist for the Composer stop button).

RUST: Register EVERY new command in the generate_handler! macro in crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs. Add #[cfg(test)] unit tests in commands.rs for the new handlers using the existing in-memory Db + InMemorySecretStore test_state() helper and the _inner pattern: e.g. get_messages returns appended messages; set_conversation_route persists the pin and clearing it (None) returns to automatic; add_mcp_server validates transport and persists; set_mcp_enabled toggles; export_conversation produces the expected shape; invalid ids/empty fields are rejected. Keep clippy -D warnings clean (scope any #[allow(dead_code)] tightly; avoid useless_vec/collapsible_if/needless_lifetimes; add doc comments carefully to avoid clippy::doc_overindented_list_items).

TS TYPES: In hybrid-orchestrator/frontend/src/types/index.ts add the exact hand-mirrored TS types for any NEW serde structs/enums that cross IPC (ExportFormat union, a ToolDescriptor display-safe shape if not already present, the route-explanation struct, McpServerInput shape for add/update). Match the Rust serde representation exactly (camelCase fields; internally-tagged unions on `type`; McpTransport env/headers as Array<[string,string]>). Do not change existing types unless a Rust type changed.

TS COMMANDS: In src/ipc/commands.ts add typed wrappers for ALL new commands (getMessages, setConversationRoute, setMessageOverride if it is a distinct command — but per Section 8.2 the per-message override is a client-side transient owned by the conversations store and passed to sendMessage's overrideRoute, so setMessageOverride may be a store action rather than an invoke; follow architecture.md Section 8.2 'Per-message override ownership' precisely), assignPersona, listMcpServers, addMcpServer, updateMcpServer, removeMcpServer, setMcpEnabled, refreshMcpTools, setToolPermission, exportConversation, openConversation, getRouteExplanation, stopGeneration. Mirror the existing wrapper style: arg object keys camelCase matching the Rust param names; JSDoc referencing the command + Section.

TS STORES (Zustand): Implement the four stores replacing the `export {};` stubs. state/conversations.ts: conversation index + active conversation id + messages for the active conversation + routing mode (auto/manual pin) + the TRANSIENT per-message override (single value owned here per Section 8.2; a setter and a consume/clear used by the Composer send path) + pending permission requests; actions to load (list_conversations/get_messages), create/rename/tag/delete, set route pin, assign persona, and reducers that apply CoreEvents (messageDelta appends to the streaming message, messageComplete finalizes route/usage/status, messageError sets error, conversationCreated/Updated/Deleted invalidate+refresh, permissionRequested enqueues, resolve dequeues). state/providers.ts: available models (list_available_models) + refresh on providersChanged. state/tools.ts: configured MCP servers + per-server connection state + tool lists; refresh on mcpStateChanged/mcpError. state/personas.ts: persona list; refresh on personasChanged. Each store exposes a plain function to feed a CoreEvent into it so a single top-level onCoreEvent subscription (wired in P5.7/app shell) can fan events out; keep the invalidate-then-refetch approach (core authoritative, Section 7.3).

TS TESTS: Extend src/ipc/commands.test.ts with the new wrappers (mocked invoke asserts command name + camelCase arg object). Add store unit tests (e.g. src/state/conversations.test.ts, providers.test.ts, tools.test.ts, personas.test.ts) that mock invoke and drive the store actions + feed synthetic CoreEvents and assert state transitions (streaming delta accumulation, completion finalize, event-driven cache invalidation). Follow the vi.mock("@tauri-apps/api/core") pattern already in commands.test.ts and vi.mock("@tauri-apps/api/event") for listen.

LOCAL VERIFY: from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` and fix all formatting (this is the only locally runnable gate). Self-audit against eslint.config.js + tsconfig.json (no unused locals/params, no explicit any, exhaustive-deps for any hooks, no fallthrough) since eslint/tsc/vitest cannot run offline. Keep every TS union that fits in 100 cols single-line.
acceptance_criteria: package.json declares a `zustand` dependency (or findings justify a local-store alternative).
src/ipc/commands.ts exports typed wrappers for every command each Section 8 surface consumes; arg object keys are camelCase matching the Rust handler param names.
The four Zustand stores are implemented (no `export {};` stubs remain) and expose actions + a CoreEvent-application function; caches invalidate/refresh on the relevant CoreEvents.

New Rust #[tauri::command] handlers exist, validate their arguments, delegate to the existing SessionManager/repos/MCP handles, return Result<_, CommandError>, and are registered in generate_handler! in lib.rs.
AppState carries a runtime MCP handle manager; send_message reads the live connected set; enabled persisted servers connect (in background) at startup.
Rust unit tests cover the new handlers via the _inner pattern; TS tests cover the new wrappers and store transitions (mocked invoke + synthetic CoreEvents).
verification: Run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend and confirm it reports all matched files use Prettier code style.

Self-audit ESLint/tsc by strict inspection against eslint.config.js and tsconfig.json (no-unused-vars/locals/params, no-explicit-any, react-hooks, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch). Report that eslint/tsc/vitest are deferred to CI (node_modules uninstallable offline).

Rust: intended `cargo test --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml` and `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings` are CI-only (crates.io offline); ensure the code is written to pass them (validated by inspection here).
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. Rust: added get_messages, set_conversation_route, assign_persona, get_route_explanation (+_inner), list/add/update/remove_mcp_server, set_mcp_enabled, refresh_mcp_tools, set_tool_permission, export_conversation (+_inner), open_conversation, stop_generation to crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs; all registered in generate_handler! in lib.rs. Added an McpRegistry (Arc<RwLock<HashMap<Uuid, Arc<McpServerHandle>>>>) plus spawn_connect/to_core_state helpers to state.rs; AppState.mcp_servers is now that registry (was a fixed empty Arc<Vec>). AppState::initialize loads persisted McpServerConfig rows, registers a handle per row, and background-connects the enabled ones (never blocks startup). send_message_inner now snapshots the LIVE registry. AppState::new (test ctor) still compiles with an empty registry. Added chrono as a dev-dependency of tauri-app (the command tests construct Message.created_at: DateTime<Utc>). Added ~13 Rust unit tests via the _inner pattern (get_messages, route pin set/clear, route-explanation precedence, add_mcp_server transport validation, enabled/permission persistence, export markdown+json shape, stop_generation validation, display-safe serde shapes).

SCOPE DECISIONS: (1) stop_generation is a VALIDATED NO-OP: the Phase 4 run_turn pipeline has no cancellation seam yet, so per the feature's allowance it validates the id/existence and returns Ok(()) so the Composer stop button has a command to call; a real cancel-flag registry is deferred. (2) set_tool_permission scopes to the per-server McpServerConfig.permission_mode: the Phase 5 mcp_servers schema has no per-tool-override column, so tool_name is accepted for forward-compat but a per-tool override is NOT persisted (documented in the command doc-comment rather than inventing a new schema). (3) set_message_override is a STORE ACTION, not an IPC command, per architecture.md Section 8.2 'Per-message override ownership' (the transient override is owned by state/conversations.ts and passed to sendMessage's overrideRoute, then cleared). (4) get_route_explanation returns a display-safe PREVIEW from persisted state (pin > persona default > last message route metadata > plain automatic) rather than a heavy dry-run route resolution, as the feature permits.

Frontend: added zustand ^4.5.5 to package.json dependencies (NOT installed locally; CI resolves it). Added typed wrappers for all new commands + listAvailableModels to src/ipc/commands.ts. Mirrored new serde types (McpServerInput, ToolDescriptorView, RouteExplanation, ExportFormat, OpenedConversation) into src/types/index.ts. Implemented the four zustand stores (conversations/providers/tools/personas) replacing the export {} stubs; each exposes load/mutation actions plus an applyCoreEvent(event) reducer for a single top-level onCoreEvent fan-out (delta accumulation, completion finalize, error, conversation lifecycle invalidate+refetch, permission enqueue/dequeue, mcp state/error tracking, providers/personas refetch). Added TS tests: extended src/ipc/commands.test.ts with every new wrapper, and added conversations/providers/tools/personas store tests driving actions + synthetic CoreEvents.

VERIFICATION: `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend PASSES (all matched files use Prettier code style). eslint/tsc/vitest are DEFERRED to CI (no node_modules; npm registry 403 offline) and self-audited against eslint.config.js (typescript-eslint recommended: no explicit any used; no unused imports/locals) and tsconfig.json (strict, noUnusedLocals/Parameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch: every switch case returns). Rust cargo fmt/clippy/test are CI-only (crates.io unreachable offline); code written to pass them (all lines <=100 cols, format!/struct-literal args pre-wrapped rustfmt-style, no unused imports, display-safe serde tests).

REVIEW FIX (2026-09-06-000311-review.md, issue #4 — disabled MCP handle lingers): set_mcp_enabled(false) now `remove`s the handle from the McpRegistry (was: get + teardown, leaving a torn-down handle in the map that stayed in send_message's live snapshot). It mirrors remove_mcp_server (remove + teardown + Disconnected event); on re-enable the enabled branch re-inserts a fresh handle and background-connects it. crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs set_mcp_enabled. The existing set_mcp_enabled_and_permission_persist test operates on the repo directly (not the registry snapshot) so it is unaffected.

REVIEW FIX (issue #1/#2 — new CoreEvent variant): added CoreEvent::MessageStarted { conversationId, messageId, role } to crates/orchestrator-core/src/events.rs (per-variant #[serde(rename_all="camelCase")]; imported Role) and mirrored it into the TS CoreEvent union in frontend/src/types/index.ts. Added a message_started_round_trips_camel_case unit test and updated the module doc + variant-count comment (eleven -> twelve). The frontend conversations store (state/conversations.ts) gained a `messageStarted` case in applyCoreEvent that appends a placeholderMessage (empty text; status 'complete' for user, 'streaming' for assistant) keyed on the event's messageId when the conversation is active, guarded against duplicate ids and ignored for non-active conversations. This closes the blocking streaming gap: the deltas/complete now land on a seeded message instead of being dropped by appendDelta's not-found guard.

VERIFY: prettier re-checked PASSES. Rust build/clippy/test deferred to CI.

REVIEW FIX v2 (2026-09-06-001627-review.md) ISSUE #2 (minor) stale #[allow(dead_code)] on CoreEvent: the enum carried an enum-level #[allow(dead_code)] with a comment saying the variants are constructed 'in later Phase 1/2 work (FEAT-003)', but MessageStarted and the message/conversation-update variants are now actually constructed by the pipeline, making the attribute + comment misleading. Audited every CoreEvent variant's construction sites across the workspace (grep for CoreEvent::<Variant> excluding events.rs): CONSTRUCTED — MessageStarted (pipeline.rs), MessageDelta (pipeline.rs), MessageComplete (pipeline.rs), MessageError (pipeline.rs), ConversationUpdated (pipeline.rs), McpStateChanged (state.rs, commands.rs), McpError (tools_bridge.rs, state.rs, commands.rs), PermissionRequested (permission.rs); STILL UNCONSTRUCTED — ConversationCreated, ConversationDeleted, ProvidersChanged, PersonasChanged (no emitter wired yet). Because four variants are genuinely still unconstructed, removing the allow entirely would trip dead_code under clippy -D warnings, so the fix NARROWS it: removed the enum-level #[allow(dead_code)] and its inaccurate comment, replaced the module-doc paragraph with an accurate note, and added a tight per-variant #[allow(dead_code)] (with a 'no emitter wired yet' comment) to ONLY the four still-unconstructed variants. crates/orchestrator-core/src/events.rs. An unnecessary allow does not trip -D warnings, and the per-variant allows are needed for the non-test build where those four variants have no constructor. VERIFY: Rust fmt/build/clippy -D warnings/test deferred to CI (crates.io offline); written to pass by inspection. Prettier unaffected (no frontend change in this issue).
